Proof. Assume, as the figure shows, that the altitude feet M (on AB) and N (on AC) lie on the sides, and that S lies inside the triangle on segments CM and BN. Statements and reasons:
1. ∠MSB = 40° — given.
2. Points M, S, C are collinear with S between M and C, so ∠MSB and ∠BSC form a linear pair — definition of linear pair. Therefore ∠BSC = 180° − 40° = 140°.
3. In ΔSBC, ∠SBC = 20° — given. The angle sum of a triangle is 180°, so ∠SCB = 180° − 140° − 20° = 20°.
4. S lies on segment CM, so ray CS = ray CM and ∠BCM = ∠SCB = 20° — same angle.
5. CM ⊥ AB, so ∠BMC = 90° — definition of altitude. In right triangle BMC, ∠MBC = 90° − ∠BCM = 90° − 20° = 70° — angle sum of a triangle.
6. M lies on side AB, so ray BM = ray BA and ∠ABC = ∠MBC = 70°.
7. S lies on segment BN, so ray BS = ray BN and ∠NBC = ∠SBC = 20° — same angle.
8. BN ⊥ AC, so ∠BNC = 90° — definition of altitude. In right triangle BNC, ∠NCB = 90° − ∠NBC = 90° − 20° = 70° — angle sum of a triangle.
9. N lies on side AC, so ray CN = ray CA and ∠ACB = ∠NCB = 70°.
10. ∠ABC = ∠ACB = 70° — from steps 6 and 9, transitivity of equality.
11. In ΔABC, sides opposite equal angles are equal — converse of the isosceles triangle theorem. Since ∠ABC = ∠ACB, side AC = side AB.
12. Therefore ΔABC is isosceles (with AB = AC), which is what we were to prove. ∎

“ΔABC is isosceles.”

Give geometric reasons for statements in your proof.

A triangle ABC with vertex A at the top, vertex B at the bottom left, and vertex C at the bottom right. Segment BN is an altitude drawn from B to AC, with a right-angle symbol at N. The angle SBC is marked with an arc and labeled 20°.

  - Correct proof. Proves that ∠B = ∠C using the following facts:

• the sum of angles in any triangle is 180°.
• if two angles of a triangle are equal, the triangle is isosceles.
and possibly also uses:
• vertically opposite angles are equal.
• supplementary angles add to 180°.
The concept of congruence is not used.
  - As code 20 but somewhere in the proof uses the fact that some triangles: e.g. triangles BCM and CBN, OR triangles BMS and CNS, are congruent.
  - All other fully correct and complete proofs.

  - Other responses with minor errors.

  - Incorrect argumentation and/or includes more than one incorrect geometric fact, step, or reason.
  - "Proof" is circular; makes use of statements which are equivalent to what is to be proven.
  - Other incorrect responses.
- Nonresponse (0 points):
  - Crossed-out, illegible, or impossible to interpret.
